clue.text: Greek torment, not exactly nice

indicators.note: something not exactly as stated is a little off, so the word that follows is rearranged

blocks.note: hell is torment or agony
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a Greek torment rather less than pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenic is the formal adjective for things relating to Greece and its people.

clue.text: A collection of animals, no tail in view, in the distance

indicators.note: with no tail the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a farm is where a collection of livestock is kept

explanation.surface: A herd of animals is glimpsed far off, their tails out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or from a great distance, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Receivers should not be sat on too long

definitions.text: should not be sat on too long

blocks.note: first meaning: people who handle stolen goods

blocks.clueFragment: should not be sat on too long
blocks.note: second meaning: barriers, from the idiom about sitting on one and refusing to take sides

explanation.walkthrough: 'Receivers' suggests radios or telephones, but here it is the criminal slang for dealers in stolen property. 'Sitting on the fence' means staying undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a fence buys and sells stolen goods, and garden fences are what indecisive people proverbially sit on.

clue.text: Roman emperor, not altogether calm, getting one Gaul destroyed

indicators.note: not altogether means not the complete word, so its end is dropped
something destroyed is broken up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the word itself, cut short
Roman numeral one
the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An agitated Roman emperor has a Gaul killed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaul, a Celt from ancient France, fits the Roman scene perfectly, which hides that its letters are to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Caligula was the notoriously cruel third emperor of Rome, reigning from AD 37 to 41.

clue.text: French friend has the talent to show cordiality

blocks.note: ami is French for friend
ability is talent or skill

explanation.surface: A French friend has a gift for being warm and welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiability is friendliness and good nature, a near synonym of cordiality.

clue.text: Being bad-tempered, Eleanor needs us to retire first

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the whole string is read from its end first

blocks.note: Nell is a short form of Eleanor
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eleanor is grumpy and wants everyone to go to bed early.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to Eleanor and us together, not to us alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen describes a sulky, bad-tempered mood, so being sullen is being bad-tempered.

clue.text: Strongest beer unfinished at short fiesta

indicators.note: unfinished means the word stops before its last letter
short means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the word itself, cut short
the word itself, cut short

explanation.surface: Someone orders the strongest beer at a brief party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strongest beer' reads as one phrase, but only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means muscular and powerful, so the beefiest is the strongest.

clue.text: Vagabonds: upmarket, note

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the next word runs backwards

blocks.note: split as up plus market; a mart is a market, and the up turns it round
PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A list of words for vagrants: upmarket, note this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upmarket' looks like one word meaning posh; split it into up and market.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless wanderers, the same people as vagabonds.

clue.text: Protection of a Royal Marine belonging to us

blocks.note: taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Our Royal Marine is shielded by his kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is a protective covering, a direct synonym for protection.

clue.text: Drink noisily (not quietly) and speak unclearly

indicators.note: not here says the following letter is to be left out of the word

blocks.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a drink loudly and then mumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: To slur is to run words together indistinctly, as a drunk person does.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp has one plan, which is kind

blocks.note: Mrs Mopp, a cleaning lady in a 1940s radio comedy, is a char, a hired cleaner
Roman numeral one
a table is a scheme or schedule set out in order

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady has a generous scheme in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp was the charlady in the wartime BBC radio show ITMA; a char is a British word for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means generous and lenient towards others, a synonym of kind.

clue.text: Spiritual knowledge is breaking into song making a comeback

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one word goes within another
a comeback runs back the way it came, so the result reads backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, placed after the first letter

explanation.surface: A spiritual awakening bursts into song as a singer returns to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is mystical or esoteric knowledge of spiritual truth, a Greek word for knowing.

clue.text: Digging support round a run-down building

indicators.note: round means going around the outside, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a sling supports an injured arm
a hovel is a squalid, run-down dwelling

explanation.surface: Excavation shores up the area around a derelict building.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovelling is moving earth with a spade-like tool, a form of digging.

clue.text: What makes tripe run blue?

indicators.note: asking what something makes invites building a new word from the letters given

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what turns rubbish into something smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour but means indecent or risqué, as in blue films.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an excessive interest in sexual matters, which matches blue in its sense of lewd.

clue.text: Credit (very large) by a crooner?

definitions.note: a definition by example, hence the question mark

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
OS, outsize, is the clothing label for very large
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge credit is paid to a lounge singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner, so his surname is an example of a smooth popular singer.

clue.text: Fish could be very tired

blocks.note: first meaning: coated in a flour mixture before frying
second meaning: worn out and exhausted, as if beaten

explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips shops coat fish in batter; the same word describes someone knocked about by fatigue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dipped in batter for cooking, and also worn out or beaten down by hard use.

clue.text: Duty of a king in a squabble

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
taken as written
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is caught up in a quarrel over import duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' only joins: 'a' and 'king' sit inside the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax charged on imports or exports, which is a customs duty.

clue.text: Uncle's wife ran off outside and thus displayed emotion

indicators.note: outside places one piece around the other

blocks.note: fled means ran off
an uncle's wife is an aunt

explanation.surface: An aunt bolts from the house, making a show of her feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife comes first in the clue but goes inside the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to show off conspicuously, so flaunted emotion is emotion paraded openly.

clue.text: Making any girl nearly bald, like Rosemary

indicators.note: nearly means almost all of the word, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: her refers to any female
the word itself, cut short

explanation.surface: A girl called Rosemary is losing her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a girl's name, but it is the plant; the capital letter disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a culinary herb, so it is herbal in nature.

clue.text: An insect gets released inside but this one is missing

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article a
a bee is an insect
sent as in sent out or let go

explanation.surface: An insect is let loose but has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is missing from where they are expected to be.

clue.text: Look! An unending hold used in bed!

indicators.note: unending means without an end, so the last letter is dropped
used in places one piece within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the word itself, cut short

explanation.surface: A wrestler's endless grip in bed, cried out in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an archaic imperative meaning look or see, used as an exclamation.

clue.text: This springtime festival is a cry for help

blocks.note: first meaning: the first of May, a traditional spring holiday
second meaning: the international radio distress call

explanation.walkthrough: The radio distress call comes from French m'aidez, help me, and happens to match the spring festival's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the May festival and the spoken signal used by ships and aircraft in distress.

clue.text: Short time taken to find one piece of fruit in me

indicators.note: in places one group of letters within another

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one
a nut is a kind of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone takes a moment to discover a bit of fruit inside themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds, a commonly used expression for a short time.

clue.text: Footballers' hairstyle might take the cake

blocks.note: first meaning: a bun worn by a player for Chelsea, the London football club
second meaning: a rolled currant bun glazed with sugar

explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club; the joke reads its name plus a hair bun. 'Take the cake' is also an idiom for being outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional British sweet spiral bun with currants, a kind of cake, and literally a bun hairstyle on a Chelsea player.

clue.text: Composer who's near collapse

indicators.note: something that collapses falls apart, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer is on the verge of a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, best known for writing Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: What's drunk when sales don't open

indicators.note: if the word does not open, its first letter is taken away

blocks.note: the word itself, without its opening

explanation.surface: Shoppers drink when the sales fail to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, the things drunk in a pub.

clue.text: Cricket stroke? Take a look!

blocks.note: first meaning: a deft deflection of the ball with an angled bat
second meaning: to look quickly

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the glance is a shot that deflects the ball fine to the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a brief look and a cricket shot that turns the ball off the bat's face.

clue.text: Boy there inside, ready for a shave

indicators.note: inside places one word within another

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy is in the bathroom, foamed up and ready to shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathered means covered with soapy foam, as a face is before shaving.
